content.text: I reviewed every input file, all six figure briefs, the numeral table, and every section of the draft against the disclosure and the USER passages in the conversation.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced; no untraced technical matter or verified internal inconsistency found. (1) Claims: every limitation of independent claims 1, 11 and 16 and of dependent claims 2-10, 12-15 and 17-20 was traced to an exact affirmative passage — rigid base with first/second sides, motor coupled to the first side, air-extraction mechanism coupled to the first side and in fluid communication with a chamber on the second side ("An air-extraction mechanism, such as a vacuum pump, is also coupled to the first side and is in fluid communication with a chamber located on a second side of the base"); rigid low-friction perimeter member at the perimeter of the second side and its materials ("formed as a rigid loop or skirt made from a low-friction material such as plastic, metal, PTFE, or a combination of rigid materials"); non-sealing behaviour, freedom from rubber/elastomer/foam and the clearance admitting ambient air ("is not intended to form a complete airtight seal and does not rely on flexible rubber or foam... it restricts airflow into the chamber while maintaining rigid contact with the tile"); continuous extraction and sub-atmospheric chamber ("continuously removes air entering beneath the rigid perimeter, maintaining the chamber at a lower pressure than the surrounding atmosphere"); operator-free holding force ("holds the device firmly against the tile without requiring the operator to press downward"); all-rigid vibration path with no resilient member ("connected to the tile through rigid components, vibration energy is transferred with substantially less damping than through a flexible suction cup"); slidability while held ("the low-friction perimeter allows the device to slide freely across different areas of the tile while the vacuum continuously maintains contact"); handle for guiding; rope/wire/cable pulling element and decoupled control; and claim 10's stirring elements and constant forward motion, which trace to the USER passage "we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion" and "we don't even need to pull or move it with the hand". No operational "resume/finalize/tighten" instruction and no YOU passage was used as support. (2) Numerals: all seventeen entries (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) appear in the detailed description, each carries one meaning across all six briefs (24 is the band/loop/legs/ring/column, all the perimeter member; 36 is the tile/band in FIGS. 1, 2, 4, 5; 10 is the whole machine in FIGS. 1, 5, 6), and every numeral used on a sheet is defined in the table. (3) Figure briefs and drawing description: the six briefs and the six Brief Description paragraphs agree on what is sectioned, what is in elevation and what is omitted (FIG. 2 hatches base, perimeter member and covering element with the air-extraction housing unhatched, matching "the base, the chamber, the perimeter member and the covering element being shown in section and the air-extraction mechanism carried on the first side of the base being shown in elevation, the vibration motor and the handle being omitted"). Section designations repeat identically in all three places: FIG. 3 carries numeral 2 at both ends of the horizontal line and numeral 4 at both ends of the vertical line, FIG. 2 is "taken on line 2-2 of FIG. 3", FIG. 4 is "taken on line 4-4 of FIG. 3", and the drawing description recites the same designations. Depiction choices are confined to the briefs and are covered by disclaimers there (rectangular slab, closed loop, ring width, block order and spacing, port width/position/form, band depths, flat lower end of the perimeter member, stirring-element number/form/position); no brief verbalises taper, angle, runout, which end is deeper, circumferential position, extent of contact or material-specific hatching, and FIG. 4 expressly asserts no extent of contact and no particular bearing-face shape. Depths and the clearance are declared schematic or "shown enlarged for clarity", matching the description. (4) Application text: the Brief Description uses only "shown schematically"/"omitted for clarity" recitals and nowhere adds a "by way of example", "any closed outline" or other optional embodiment to justify a renderer's choice; the description and claims remain shape- and location-neutral for the handle, the pulling-element connection and the stirring elements. (5) Text checks: claims and description use the same terms and relationships (bearing face as end face, clearance along at least part, pressure differential maintained during translation, decoupled control); the Background's two-problem framing has proper antecedents and its prior-art characterisations were left for the citation review; no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction to a person, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any section; title, cross-reference and government-support text match the filing brief.
